splits.en: When you first signed up for a course in university, like a psychology course, chances are that you didn’t really expect what was coming in your study; particularly, the course emphasis on methodology and statistics.
zh: 刚在大学选修一门课，比如心理学时，
你很可能并没有真正预料到将要学习什么，
尤其没有想到课程会强调研究方法和统计学。

splits.en: No doubt in other parts of your course study, you will read books and journals, examining, critically, models and theories, assumptions and hypotheses put forward by scholars and specialists.
zh: 毫无疑问，在课程学习的其他部分，你们会阅读书籍和期刊，
批判性地考察学者和专家提出的模型、理论、假设和假说。

splits.en: My task today is to help you understand some of the important features of experimental reports, because you will have to write up some kind of report of this nature if your course gives prominence to practical work, especially experimenting.
zh: 我今天的任务是帮助你们了解实验报告的一些重要特点，
因为如果课程重视实践，尤其是实验，你们就必须撰写这类报告。

splits.en: In doing this, you are more like an ancient storyteller, whose stories were structured in accordance with widely recognized and long-established conventions, than a modern novelist who is free to dictate form as well as content.
zh: 写报告时，你更像古代的说书人，要按照公认且历史悠久的惯例来组织故事，
而不像可以自由决定形式与内容的现代小说家。

splits.en: Moreover, like the storyteller of old, although you will invariably be telling your story to someone who knows quite a bit about it already, you are expected to present it as if it had never been heard before.
zh: 而且，像旧时的说书人一样，尽管你总是在向已经相当了解这个故事的人讲述，
仍然应当把它当作一个从未被听过的故事来讲。

splits.en: In reality, however, the marker will be assessing your report on behalf of someone else—an idealized, hypothetical person who is intelligent but unknowledgeable about your study and the area in which it took place.
zh: 然而，实际上，评分人是在代另一个人评估报告：
这是一个理想化、假想的读者，虽然聪明，却不了解你的研究及其所属领域。

splits.en: In short, you should write for someone who knows little about your area of study, taking little for granted about your reader’s knowledge of your area of study.
zh: 简而言之，你应当为不了解研究领域的人写作，
不要想当然地认为读者具备相关知识。

splits.en: If you find this difficult to do, then a useful approach is to write the report as if it will be read by someone you know who is intelligent but unknowledgeable about your subject.
zh: 如果你觉得这很难做到，一个有用的办法是：写报告时，
想象读者是你认识的某个人，虽聪明，却不了解你的研究课题。

splits.en: At this early stage, you will be expected mainly to show that you understand what you did in your report and its implications, together with evidence that you have, at least, a basic grasp of the demands of the report’s format.
zh: 在这个早期阶段，你主要需要表明自己理解报告中做了什么及其意义，
同时证明自己至少基本掌握了报告格式的要求。

splits.en: The “why you did it” part will become more important because, in being responsible for the choice of topic and design, you will be expected to be able to justify this choice.
zh: “为什么这样做”会变得更重要，
因为既然你要对选题和设计负责，就需要能够说明这种选择的合理性。

splits.en: You will need, therefore, to develop the habit of thinking about how the ideas that you are entertaining for your experiment or study will look in the report, paying particular attention to how they will fit into the part of INTRODUCTION.
zh: 因此，你要养成一种习惯：思考实验或研究中正在考虑的想法，在报告中该如何呈现，
尤其要关注它们如何融入“引言”部分。

splits.en: And second, the undertaking of a project that lacks any research justification, because it is based on assumptions that are contradicted by existing findings in the area.
zh: 第二，所开展的项目缺乏研究上的正当理由，
因为其依据的假设，与该领域已有的研究发现相矛盾。

splits.en: OK. Today we’ve had a brief look at the format of an experimental report, what each section is about and some of the basic issues like reader awareness, so on and so forth.
zh: 好，今天我们简要了解了实验报告的格式、
各节的内容，以及读者意识等一些基本问题。

splits.en: By becoming involved in Toastmasters, you will learn different methods of communicating what you really want to say, and equally important, you will learn what your audience expects from you so you can deliver that message to them in a logical fashion.
zh: 加入国际演讲会后，你会学到不同的方法来表达自己真正想说的内容；
同样重要的是，你还会了解听众的期待，从而有条理地向他们传达信息。

splits.en: Yes, different assignments within Toastmasters involve not only preparation of speeches and then presenting these before an audience, but also the opportunity of serving as toastmaster of the meeting.
zh: 是的，国际演讲会安排的不同任务，不仅包括准备演讲并在听众面前发表，
还包括担任会议主持人的机会。

splits.en: Other assignments include serving as an evaluator for another speaker, or serving as grammarian who will monitor use of filler words or phrases, such as “and”, “uh”, “er” or “you know”.
zh: 其他任务包括为另一位演讲者担任评估员，
或者担任语言监督员，留意“and”“uh”“er”“you know”等填充词或短语的使用。

splits.en: As an individual continues to give speeches and improve, he progresses from the point of being fearful to stand before a group of peers to the point where he can address any group of people with a degree of self-confidence.
zh: 随着一个人不断演讲、不断进步，他会从害怕站到一群同辈面前，
逐步成长为能够带着一定自信向任何一群人讲话的人。
